newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa truth commission subpoenas nine policemen.
newsitem.headline: South Africa truth commission subpoenas nine policemen.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission on Tuesday subpoenaed nine policemen in connection with the 1986 killing of seven black youths alleged to be trained African National Congress (ANC) guerrillas.

The most prominent policemen in the group are Director Leonard Knipe, who heads a specialised police unit dealing with gangs in Western Cape province, and the region's police spokesman, Senior Superintendent John Sterrenberg.

"In terms of the subpoenas, they are required to produce before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission such evidence as video and sound recordings in their possession which may be relevant to the hearing," commission spokeswoman Christelle Terreblanche said in a statement.

The seven youths were ambushed by police in Guguletu, a black township outside Cape Town. Police reports at the time said they were armed with automatic rifles and had been planning to attack a police station.
But in May this year, parents of the so-called Guguletu Seven told the commission their children had been unarmed and asked for an investigation.

The commission was formed last year and is chaired by Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu. Its job is to uncover human rights violations under apartheid and it has power to grant amnesty to violators who come clean.
Former apartheid-era security police operatives have generally been reluctant to approach the commission for amnesty. In response, the commission has resorted to subpoenaing them.
